items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: Herbie said he was coming out in a couple of months or something, on his way to Japan and would I join him to go there and work a gig in Japan.

ctx.x: In the meantime, just before I left Los Angeles, I got a call from Herbie Mann. Herbie said he was coming out in a couple of months or something, on his way to Japan and would I join him to go there and work a gig in Japan. I had never been in Japan -- still haven't -- and I was saying, 'Wow, this is great.' But I told Herbie, I said, 'Herbie, call me back a little later. I can't answer that now because I've got some things pending. And if you haven't found anybody in the next few weeks, call me again closer to…

But I knew right then that I wasn't ready to just start accepting jobs, even going to Japan, which I always wanted to do. And working with Herbie wasn't a drag, but I just couldn't get my head together.

So when I went to San Francisco, to the Bay Area, I didn't want anybody to know I was there because I didn't want to do anything. Had to get my head together, I knew that. I put my instrument in the shop. So I was dealing with a musical problem and a family problem: musical insofar as what I was going to do in the future.
